premiseVerifiedAtSource.planRow: P-298 (90_operations/OPS-16_texas_market_plan_of_record.md, read at origin/main 20204af9): 'THE GATE SCHEDULER READS A WHOLE COUNTY PER RAIL, SO A COLD CACHE TURNS AN HOURLY JOB INTO A HALF-DAY ONE; AND IT TAKES NO LEASE.' premiseVerifiedAtSource.measuredFinding: A-196 (same file, same commit): the per-rail page query in src/lib/parcel-record-engine/load.js runs on parcel_record_cell_pkey (place_key, rail_key), so every rail pass walks every rail's index entries in the county's range (about 24.7M for Travis, whose 380,917 parcels carry 65 rails each) to return one rail's. Warm, the six counties took 33 minutes; cold, Travis took about six minutes PER RAIL on Neon/PS_ReadIO.
readAndConfirmedInTheClone: src/lib/parcel-record-engine/load.js loadCountyRailCellsPage: exactly the query P-298 quotes, `WHERE place_key > $1 AND place_key < $2 AND rail_key = $3 ORDER BY place_key LIMIT $4`, page size DEFAULT_RAIL_CELL_PAGE_SIZE = 500, and the page loop is `after = lastRow.place_key` until a short page -- so the county range is walked once per rail, not per parcel.

src/lib/parcel-record-engine/load.js loadCountyRailCells asserts cells.length === parcel_record row count for the county and THROWS on a mismatch, so 380,917 cells per rail are loaded for Travis: 762 pages per rail at page size 500. That is the multiplier A-196 measured.

migrations/0007_parcel_record.sql (verbatim engine schema): parcel_record_cell PRIMARY KEY (place_key, rail_key); existing indexes are parcel_record_cell_pkey, parcel_record_cell_rail_idx (rail_key) and parcel_record_cell_unaccounted_idx (place_key) WHERE cell_state->>'kind' = 'unaccounted'. An index on (rail_key) alone cannot serve the ORDER BY place_key LIMIT without a sort, and cannot avoid reading every matching row; hence the pair ordering (rail_key, place_key).

src/db/migrate.mjs: applyMigrations wraps every file in `BEGIN` ... `COMMIT`, so CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot live in migrations/ -- it would abort the whole migrate job with 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block' and the index would never exist. Confirmed by reading the file, not assumed.

src/jobs/publish-gate-sched.mjs: the apply path connects with connectFactory(env) and computes RAIL_LIVENESS_SQL ONCE per run (P-195, one full-table scan over parcel_record_cell); every (county, rail) pair then shells out to the vendored gate CLI, which runs the paged per-rail read in a SUBPROCESS. So the run's scans are this process's liveness scan PLUS its children's page loops -- the lease must cover both, which it does because the children inherit this process's window.

item1_theIndex.what: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS parcel_record_cell_rail_place_idx ON parcel_record_cell (rail_key, place_key).
item1_theIndex.whyNotInMigrations: migrations/ is transactional (src/db/migrate.mjs). The step is therefore a separate, clearly named non-transactional artifact: sql/p298/0015_parcel_record_cell_rail_place_idx.sql, executed by scripts/p298-build-rail-place-index.mjs. A test asserts the file carries exactly one statement, that it is CONCURRENTLY, and that it is NOT under migrations/ -- so a later 'tidy-up' that moves it into the migrate job fails a test instead of aborting every migration behind it.
item1_theIndex.whyThisKeyOrder: (rail_key, place_key): equality on the leading column, then a range scan in place_key order that satisfies ORDER BY place_key LIMIT 500 without a sort and without walking sibling rails. (place_key, rail_key) is what the primary key already is. A partial index per rail was rejected: 65 indexes to maintain under a writer that rewrites cells.
item1_theIndex.noIncludeClause: INCLUDE (cell_state) was rejected: cell_state is a jsonb of roughly 100-300 bytes, so an index-only-scan index would be larger than the heap it duplicates (~18GB) and would double the writer's cost. The page read takes a heap fetch either way.
item1_theIndex.estimatesFromTheTablesOwnStatistics: read-only, via pg_class/page-size and pg_stats: entry count = parcel_record_cell.reltuples; entry width = 16 (btree tuple header with page offset) + max(place_key avg_width, rail_key avg_width) pairs as their true types (text, 4-byte varlena header) + item pointers; the same-key-columns cross-check is parcel_record_cell_pkey's own size, since the new index carries the identical tuple set in a different order.
item1_theIndex.whatTheLaneWillNotDo: no CREATE INDEX and no DDL of any kind against any fleet store; the index is BUILT on the scratch container only, to produce the plans and the build-rate measurement. The integration seat builds it on the real store with the command this lane hands over.

item2_thePlanProof.method: The exact production query text, EXPLAINed on the scratch rig at the two counties' real row counts, before the index exists (baseline, expected to name parcel_record_cell_pkey) and after (expected to name parcel_record_cell_rail_place_idx), with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, VERBOSE, BUFFERS) beside it so the difference is stated in shared hits/reads as well as in milliseconds. A full rail pass is timed by paging exactly as load.js pages.
item2_thePlanProof.ifThePlannerStillPrefersThePkey: then the smallest query change is to add `rail_key`-equality-first index hints -- Postgres has no hints, so the real candidate is a query rewrite that the planner cannot mis-cost, and it would be a VENDORED DIVERGENCE recorded in ENGINE_PIN.json exactly as P-252 recorded its own (files list, what/why/howToRetire/engineSideStatus) plus a new EXPECTED_DIVERGENCE entry in test/engine-pin-divergence.test.mjs. That path is only taken if the measurement demands it; the falsifier is pre-registered below so the outcome cannot be chosen afterwards.
item2_thePlanProof.notClaimed: no plan is claimed against the live store: this lane has no credential for it, and the dispatch reserves the live grading (and the cold six-county run) to the integration seat.

item3_theLease.hookPoints: grantHeavyScanLease before any read of the factory store (before RAIL_LIVENESS_SQL and before the first subprocess), attachRun(runId) after startRun on the apply path, assertHeld() at each (county, rail) boundary inside the loop, close({outcome}) in the finally BEFORE the connection is ended -- the ordering parcel-envelope-cells.mjs already uses, because a release after the connection closes has nowhere to land.
item3_theLease.storeKey: storeRefFromEnv(env, 'FACTORY_DATABASE_URL'), i.e. the connection HOST, which is exactly what the job's own connectFactory(env) connects to and what the lease module keys on.
item3_theLease.windowAndHolder: windowKind 'heavy-scan'; holder from leaseHolder(env) so a Cloud Run execution names its execution and a local run says it is a seat; ttlMs from ttlMsFromEnv(env).
item3_theLease.refusalSemantics: LEASE_HELD propagates as a refusal with no run row (the lease is taken BEFORE startRun, so a refused scan never leaves a run row claiming work that never started -- P-281's own stated reason for that ordering). No wait/retry loop: the dispatch's falsifier 2 asks for a refusal, and for an hourly job the next tick is the retry.
item3_theLease.amendmentToExistingBehaviour_thisIsTheOn: A DRY RUN NOW TAKES THE LEASE, and therefore now requires FACTORY_DATABASE_URL. Today a dry run opens no factory connection at all and lets each subprocess connect for itself -- and those subprocesses perform the SAME page loops, so a dry run is a heavy scan with no lease. AGENT_CONTRACT section 4 has no dry-run exemption. The property this changes is the one test/publish-gate-sched.test.mjs names 'no forced DB connection just to preview'; what P-195 actually needed is preserved and re-asserted: a dry run STILL omits --declared-ahead, so it still does not compute the program-wide liveness scan in this process. Net: a preview of the store is a scan of the store and says so.
item3_theLease.knownCostLeftOpen: on a dry run each subprocess computes the program-wide liveness scan for itself (the CLI's own fallback), so a 6-county x 65-rail dry run performs 390 full-table scans of parcel_record_cell. That is a bigger cost than the per-rail reads this row is about, it is inside the leased window after this lane, and it is REPORTED here as a finding rather than fixed: fixing it means computing declaredAhead on a dry run, which is a behaviour change P-195 chose deliberately and which this mission does not ask for.

item4_theTimingHarness.what: scripts/p298-rail-pass-timing.mjs: read-only, requires --county and --rail, times one rail pass through the engine's own loadCountyRailCells (the production read shape, not a re-typed copy), and prints the EXPLAIN of the page query so the reader can see WHICH index served it, plus page count, total ms, median/min/max ms per page.
item4_theTimingHarness.guards: read-only session (default_transaction_read_only = on), refuses without FACTORY_DATABASE_URL by naming the variable, refuses a full pass without --confirm-heavy-scan (so a stray invocation cannot heavy-scan the store), prints the AGENT-CONTRACT section 4 announce line (target, expected duration) before the first page, and never writes.
item4_theTimingHarness.whyItExists: the dispatch's item 4: the integration seat grades the change cold and warm on the real store. What this lane can prove locally is the same instrument against the same query text; what it cannot prove is Neon's cold-cache behaviour, which stays the integration seat's measurement.

falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.falsifier: 4 (this lane's own, added because item 1's fix is DDL on an 18GB table).
falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.preRegisteredAnswer: The index step refuses to run outside its named store, refuses without --apply, issues no BEGIN, and, if a previous CONCURRENTLY build died, detects an INVALID index and prints the drop-and-retry command instead of silently succeeding on `IF NOT EXISTS`. Expected PASS, tested with a doubled client; the 'invalid index' case is the one a naive IF NOT EXISTS implementation gets wrong.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnPlan: The premise I am NOT allowed to assume is that the index alone fixes the plan. An index only gets chosen when the planner's cost model prefers it; at 26M rows with realistic statistics it should (500-entry ordered scan vs ~32,500-entry filtered walk), but the rig is the test and a FAIL is a legitimate outcome with a proposal attached -- so the falsifier is pre-registered above rather than discovered afterwards.

A CONCURRENTLY build that fails leaves an INVALID index behind which `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` then SKIPS, so the second run reports success while the query still uses the pkey. My step therefore verifies pg_index.indisvalid/indisready after the build and names the DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY remedy. Without this the lane could hand the integration seat a command that silently does nothing on the second attempt.

Refusing LEASE_HELD stops the hourly scheduler while another heavy scan holds the factory store -- the P-252 apply holds it right now (holder integration-p252-apply). That is the rule working (a second heavy scan waits, P-281 F2), but the consequence is stated: verdicts simply are not refreshed for that tick, and the allowlist fails CLOSED on a missing verdict, so no parcel is served anything new because of it.

The lease is taken before startRun, so a LEASE_HELD run leaves no run row and therefore no `runs` evidence -- only the heavy_scan_lease_refusals row. That is P-281's deliberate ordering; the lane must not 'helpfully' move the lease after startRun and thereby recreate the run-row-claims-work-that-never-ran defect.

Bastrop's plan is not Travis's problem: Bastrop has 24,988 parcels and its county range is 1/15th of Travis's, so its pkey plan is comparatively cheap. Both are measured anyway, because the falsifier names both and because a fix that only helps the biggest county is what the next cold run would find.

The census edit is the piece most likely to be judged out of scope. It is kept minimal and additive, the delta is reported as a number, and the justification is the mission's own premise being unverifiable without it.
